items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: Our piano player at that time was Bill Samual, with Roy's trumpet player, and alto player and a drummer, and myself -- and we had a girl singer. Her name was Toy Tori.

ctx.x: Jerry was managing Harry James, and he said, 'Well, you got to sign these options. We're gonna take you out to Victor Hugo's out in the West Coast.' He says, 'We're gonna give you a couple of jobs playing up there -- at the Hotel Sherman -- for smokers.' However, we signed these options and we went down there a couple of times; they had a couple of jobs while the band was still there.

And when it was time for them to leave, he had to explain that he wouldn't accept no colored out at Victor Hugo's. But we were talented, and that group broke up right then. And somebody come by my house when I was staying with Reverend Turner and said, 'You want to go to Quincy, Illinois?' A trumpet player named Roy something -- I can't remember too well, but we went down there. Our piano player at that time was Bill Samual, with Roy's trumpet player, and alto player and a drummer, and myself -- and we had a girl…

And the job was for 4 months. And every little territory band at that time had somebody who did a show. I'd get out and dance, the piano player would do his number -- everybody had a little number to do. And I'll never forget it.
